author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Apple’s first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, will start at $1,999 in the United States, placing it at the high end of an already small smartphone segment. The largest-storage version is priced at $3,199. Apple demonstrated apps including Zoom, Slack and Netflix using the expanded display and positioned the device as a personal hub for artificial intelligence.

The launch gives Apple a new form factor but leaves a central question about the size of the audience willing to pay the premium. IDC expects foldables to account for less than 3% of global smartphone shipments in 2026 and 2027. Counterpoint Research estimated Apple could sell about 6 million units by year-end, roughly a quarter of the foldable segment.

Samsung currently holds about 40% of the foldable market, giving Apple an established rival and a benchmark for durability, software and everyday usefulness. Omdia projects 22.3 million foldable shipments worldwide this year. Apple’s entry could expand consumer awareness, but its initial price means the Duo’s early performance will test whether large-screen multitasking and AI features are compelling enough to move foldables beyond a niche.
dek: Apple is pitching its first folding phone as a premium personal AI device, but analysts question how broad the audience will be at its launch price.
headline: Apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo tests the foldable market
